output.brief: The 11 November Level 2 failure looks like a one-off chance flag, not a faulty analyzer. Over 546 QC measurements since 12 October it was the only violation. The repeat passed, and the new reagent lot did not move QC means (Level 2 5.81 before, 5.80 after). Re-running 43 samples on Analyzer A matched Analyzer B within 0.1 mmol/L on average. The event log shows no instrument error, though a short sample cannot be fully excluded. Ward 6's high potassiums are split evenly between analyzers, so Analyzer B is not the clear cause. The pneumatic tube outage and long transit times are a plausible but unproven explanation. Staffing did not cause skipped QC, since all 182 runs completed. I would not recall the lot, widen limits, or record a sampling cause. I would return Analyzer B to service with extra Level 2 checks each shift for a week. Do not sign off closing the review with no amendments yet. Ward 6's high results need a repeat-sample check and a transit-time review. I am moderately confident in this, but the Ward 6 question is still open.
